name: Private credit stress
value: BCRED Q2 requests ~10% vs usual 5% cap
summary: Nontraded BDC redemption requests remain about double the usual 5% caps; no wave of simultaneous gates found
state: Client redemptions from nontraded BDCs reached $12.7bn in the first half of 2026, and Blackstone's BCRED received second-quarter requests of about 10% of shares, double its usual 5% limit (InvestmentNews, 18 Nov). Fitch said on 13 Oct that requests at 13 of 15 perpetual nontraded BDCs averaged 9.8% of shares in the third quarter, down from 10.3%, with nine funds above 5%. Searches on 28 Nov found no simultaneous gating by several large funds, no forced asset sales and no losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Holders of semi-liquid private credit funds and nontraded BDCs may have only part of a withdrawal request paid in a quarter while requests exceed caps. Bank depositors and insurance policyholders are not directly exposed on current evidence.
rubric_hit: Watch: large funds limiting redemptions (BCRED requests ~10% vs 5% cap); no multi-fund gating, forced sales or bank/insurer losses

sources.title: InvestmentNews — After a tough year, are private credit funds and BDCs in line for a comeback in 2027?
InvestmentNews — Pace of investors selling nontraded BDCs slows but remains significant, says Fitch

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
